title.en: Choose the viewing scale before building the world

summary: Settle whether the viewer holds the world or stands inside it, because that choice sets units, detail, camera range and collision needs.
objective: Make the scale and traversal decision explicit early so geometry budget and camera behaviour follow one intent.
applies_when: A new environment, diorama, town or interior is being started from a one-line brief.
The user says explore, walk around, fly over, or asks for a model on a table.
Camera controls, level of detail or object density are being chosen.
intent_signals: build a village I can explore
show me a model of the site
example_prompts: Make a tabletop diorama of the harbour I can spin and inspect.
Put me on the ground in the village at human height.
negative_signals: Single-object product or specimen views where the subject fills the frame and traversal is irrelevant.
Abstract diagram scenes with no physical scale.
not_for: Single-object product or specimen views where the subject fills the frame and traversal is irrelevant.
Abstract diagram scenes with no physical scale.

principles: Diorama and inhabited views fail in opposite directions. A diorama read from two metres away wastes budget on doorknobs; a walkable street built at diorama density looks like a bare stage at eye height.
The chosen scale sets the camera near and far planes, and a near plane too small next to a far plane too large is the usual cause of depth artefacts on distant surfaces.
Traversal mode decides how much physical machinery is needed: an orbiting diorama needs no collision at all, while walking needs support, clearance and step handling.
implementation: State the intended viewing distance in the same units as the model, then place detail where that distance can resolve it: silhouette and roof mass for a diorama, thresholds, handrails and door thickness for eye-level.
For a diorama, prefer one orbit target, a bounded zoom range and a clean base or plinth that frames the world edge instead of an infinite fade.
For an inhabited view, add eye height, walk speed, a collision body and a ground query before adding more scenery.
When both are wanted, treat them as two framed modes over one model with a transition that preserves position and selection, not as two scenes.
observable_checks: Look at the scene from the stated viewing distance only; details invisible there are budget spent in the wrong place.
Zoom to the intended extremes and watch for far-plane clipping, z-fighting on flat surfaces, and scenery pop.
In an inhabited view, walk into a doorway, a stair and a narrow alley; diorama-scale geometry usually blocks or swallows the body there.
Compare a known reference object, such as a door or a person, against buildings to expose an inconsistent scale ladder.

creative_affordances: Deliberate scale play, such as a giant standing over a miniature town, remains available; declare it so it reads as a choice.
Mixed modes, inset views and picture-in-picture overviews are all reasonable when the transition preserves state.
known_limits: Authored composition guidance; no runtime frame rate, draw-call or rendering measurement is asserted.
Does not prescribe a units convention; it requires only that one be chosen and used consistently.
